subject: RTBF/Delete request — backup purge timeline & logs (FinTechCo)
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Apr 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: RTBF / delete request — timeline & next steps

Hi Andrea / Privacy Team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to meet you. Quick recap and next steps on the RTBF/delete items we discussed: 

- Summary from call:
  - FinTechCo confirmed a potential Right-to-Be-Forgotten (RTBF) flow for a subset of test accounts and an expectation for proof of purge across active DBs, logs, and backups.
  - Key ask: whether Redwood can provide (a) deletion timelines, (b) confirmation of PII removal from logs, and (c) approach to purge from backups/resilience snapshots.

- What I promised on the call:
  1) Clarify our standard deletion timelines and caveats for backups and third-party snapshot providers.
  2) Share our RTBF workflow doc and an FAQ (attached).
  3) If needed, open an engineering ticket to estimate a guaranteed SLA for expedited purges.

Next steps: I pulled together the high-level answers below — please confirm if any of these need to be stricter for your compliance team. If yes, we can scope an SLA and an engineering change.

High-level timelines (standard):
- Active data (user profile, message content): deletion from active replicas within 72 hours after request acceptance.
- In-memory caches / KV: invalidation within 24 hours; best-effort immediate purge on expedited requests.
- Application logs: PII is redacted at ingest where possible; raw logs retained for 180 days by default, with PII obfuscation applied after 7 days.
- Backups & snapshots: backups are on a 90-day rolling retention window by default. Physical removal from backup media occurs at the next backup rotation and requires coordination with our storage provider; typical full purge can take up to 90 days from the delete request depending on snapshot retention and provider SLAs.

Attachments: RTBF_delete_workflow_v2.pdf (workflow + steps), RTBF_FAQ.xlsx (FAQ mapping to audit evidence).

If you need a more aggressive timeline (e.g., purge backups within 30 days), let me know and I will get engineering and infra scoped — we'll likely need a mutual action plan and a small change to the backup rotation or a provider-side expunge.

Thanks — I cc'd Marissa (security/compliance) and will loop Dev for engineering clarifications once you confirm desired timelines.

Best,
Camila
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Post-call: RTBF / delete request — timeline & next steps

Hi Andrea — appreciate the detailed questions. Answers below (high level) — marking items that will need engineering confirmation.

1) Backups & snapshots:
- Responsibility: Redwood initiates the purge workflow for our managed-hosted backups. For cloud-provider snapshots (e.g., managed snapshot by infra provider), we coordinate with the provider to ensure the object is expired/removed. If you have a vendor-managed backup outside Redwood's control we will provide guidance but the vendor must execute the deletion.
- Timeline: default retention is 90 days; physical removal can take up to the next backup rotation window. For an expedited workflow (customer-requested expunge), engineering will attempt to identify snapshots containing the objects and request provider-side expunge; estimate: 7-30 days depending on provider and snapshot chain complexity. This is a scoped engineering effort.

2) Logs & PII fields:
- Types considered PII in logs: email addresses, user_id, phone numbers, full-text user content (if logged).
- Redact vs delete: We support redaction (masking) at log ingest and can run a post-ingest scrub to remove PII tokens from logs. Full deletion of log lines is more complex (because logs are append-only and often stored in immutable snapshots); typical approach is to redact and then prove removal of PII via hashing/blacklist evidence.
- We can provide log-redaction proof (hashes before/after) and an export of the scrub process for audit.

3) Expedited purge for small sets (10-20 users):
- ETA (engineering-backed estimate):
  - Active DB + caches: 24-72 hours.
  - Logs (redaction + audit artifacts): 3-7 days.
  - Backups full expunge: 7-30 days (provider dependent) — requires engineering ticket and optionally provider SLA.
- Cost: if you require a guaranteed SLA (e.g., purge backups <30 days regardless of provider), we'll need to scope and provide a price for the operational work and any provider fees.

Next step proposal: I will open an internal engineering ticket (cc'ing Dev) and we can propose a mutual action plan (MAP) that lists the accounts, exact PII fields to purge, and the desired SLA. Once we have agreement we can put the MAP into DocuSign and schedule a technical call.

Marissa / Dev — tagging you for any corrections to the timelines above or if you want to propose alternative wording for the audit artifacts.

Thanks — Camila
